name: Existing Filename Sanitizer
description: Provides Drush commands to sanitize existing filenames in Drupal.
project_description: This module provides a single Drush command that renames the filenames of existing managed file entities so they match Drupal core's filename-sanitization rules. It is intended for sites that enabled core's upload-time filename sanitization (Configuration → Media → File system) but still hold legacy files uploaded before that setting was active. The command reads the same options that core stores in file.settings.filename_sanitization (transliterate, replace whitespace, replace non-alphanumeric, deduplicate separators, lowercase, replacement character) and can override each per run. It walks all permanent file entities, computes a sanitized filename, and where it differs renames both the physical file (via the file_system service, using EXISTS_RENAME so it never overwrites) and the file entity's filename/uri. A dry-run mode previews changes, and it handles temporary, missing and generated (oEmbed/cache) files gracefully. It exposes no routes, forms, permissions or configuration of its own — it is a CLI maintenance tool. Requires Drupal 10 or 11, Drush, and the core File module.
